name: Côte de Beaune

known.via: English Wikipedia "Côte de Beaune" (a wine place on Wikidata)

climate.koppen_name: Temperate, no dry season, warm summer

terms: Bourgogne, village, Premier Cru, Grand Cru
Burgundy's four levels, from regional Bourgogne up through village wines to Premier Cru and Grand Cru vineyards.
keyfacts: Pinot Noir is mainly planted around Beaune, Pommard and Volnay; Meursault, Puligny and Chassagne are mainly white, and Santenay and Maranges return to red.
Corton is the only red Grand Cru in the district, and it and the white Grand Cru Corton-Charlemagne both span Aloxe-Corton, Ladoix-Serrigny and Pernand-Vergelesses.
The Montrachet Grand Crus are split between Puligny-Montrachet and Chassagne-Montrachet and include Chevalier-Montrachet and Bâtard-Montrachet.
Côte de Beaune Villages is a general appellation for 16 villages, excluding Aloxe-Corton, Pommard, Volnay and Beaune.

notes: Reds grow lighter and more perfumed from the Côte de Nuits south through Beaune.
Meursault makes rich, buttery Chardonnay that turns nutty with time.
Corton's best reds join the muscle of the Côte de Nuits with the elegance of the Côte de Beaune.
Pommard has a solid structure with velvety fruit and long aging potential, while Volnay is prized for great finesse, its tannic frame balanced by discreet acidity.

blurb.text: The southern part of the Côte d'Or limestone ridge, about ⟦dist|15 miles|24 km⟧ long. Reds continue from the Côte de Nuits but are lighter and more perfumed. Farther south lie great white names like Meursault and Chassagne-Montrachet.
